item.title: Topological Lifting of Mundici Equivalence and Di Nola--Lettieri Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2611.10087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that summability characterises precisely when a topological MV-algebra can be realized as the unit interval of a lattice-ordered topological abelian group, thereby providing a topological lifting of both Mundici equivalence and DiNola--Lettieri equivalence. Applications include a Birkhoff--Kakutani-type metrisation theorem, a second-countability criterion, and a topological extension of a key continuity lemma from the proof theory of first-order {\L}ukasiewicz logic---following Baaz--Metcalfe's hypersequent approach to approximate completenesss---and provides an $A$-valued topological semantics for the approximate strong completeness of~$\mathbf{G}\text{{\L}}\forall$, where $A$ ranges over summable topological MV-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Yichuan Yang

item.title: Rigid Lie Algebras from Semisimple Lie Algebras and Their Symplectic Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.10747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider two extensions associated with a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic module $V$ over a complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{s}$, and study their rigidity. The toral extension adjoins a derivation acting as the identity on $V$ and trivially on $\mathfrak{s}$; the Heisenberg extension uses the invariant symplectic form on $V$ to define a central bracket. For the toral extension, we compute the first and second adjoint cohomology groups in terms of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{s}}(V)$, and obtain rigidity precisely when $V$ is irreducible. These results hold for arbitrary nonzero finite-dimensional modules. For the Heisenberg extension, we express the second adjoint cohomology as the kernel of a map combining the symplectic centralizer with an equivariant Jacobi map. A Killing-form argument shows that every multiplicity-free sum of irreducible symplectic modules gives an algebraically rigid Heisenberg extension. We also treat constructions with independent toral generators or Heisenberg centers. Repeated summands lead to explicit nonrigid examples, including a deformation to $\mathfrak{sl}_3$. The proofs use invariant cochains and recover several previously studied families.
item.dc:creator: Estela Fern\'andez, Paulo Tirao

item.title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.10788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-depth; this depth governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of depth at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has depth at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.
item.dc:creator: Vu A. Le, Hoa Q. Duong, Tuan A. Nguyen

item.title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.11082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the interval between the varieties generated by the nonempty and full power semirings of a semigroup satisfying \(xy\approx x^2\). It has two elements for a one-element semigroup, three for a nontrivial left-zero or null semigroup, and seven otherwise, without any finiteness assumption. In the seven-element case the interval is \([\Rvar,\Rvar^0]\), where \(\Rvar=\Mod_{\rm ai}\{xy\approx xz\}\) and \(\Rvar^0\) is its zero-adjunction variety. Every word absorption valid in \(\Rvar\) but not in \(\Rvar^0\) is equivalent over \(\Rvar^0\) to one of six relative identities. We give exact absorption criteria and finite bases for all seven varieties. Three have basis rank two and four have basis rank three; their two-generated free algebras have orders \(15\), \(24\), or \(35\). We also count the finite-rank free algebras of both endpoints.
item.dc:creator: Aifa Wang, Lili Wnag, Qingrui Yin

item.title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.11168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Guilai Liu, Chengming Bai, Li Guo

item.title: Inverse problem in difference Galois theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $K=C(x)$ with $\sigma(x)=x+1$. We show that every closed subgroup $G\subseteq\GL_n(C)$ with cyclic component group $G/G^\circ$ can be realized as the \PV{} group of a system $\sigma Y=A(x)Y$. Here $G^\circ$ denotes the identity component of $G$. Moreover, we can choose the coefficient matrix to have the formal expansion $A(x)=h+O(x^{-2})$ at infinity, where $h\in G(C)$ is semisimple. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture of van der Put and Singer in their monograph \emph{Galois Theory of Difference Equations} (Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol.~1666). The original results in this paper were entirely generated by ChatGPT 6 and the MechMath Agent Team (MMAT) developed by the Key Laboratory of Mathematics Mechanization, AMSS, CAS. The author reviewed and simplified the initial proofs and verified the correctness of the results.
item.dc:creator: Ruyong Feng

item.title: Linear bound for commuting matrix algebra II
item.description: arXiv:2611.11550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field, and let $A_1,\cdots,A_m$ be pairwise commuting $n\times n$ matrices. For $m\geq3$ and $n\geq2$, we prove \[ \dim_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{F}[A_1,\cdots,A_m] \leq \left\lceil C_m(n-1)\right\rceil \quad\text{with}\quad C_m=\frac{\Gamma(m)}{\Gamma((m+1)/2)^2}. \] In particular, three commuting matrices generate an algebra of dimension at most $2n-2$.
item.dc:creator: Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng

item.title: Lift Height and the Structure of Classification Failure
item.description: arXiv:2611.11611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a framework for measuring the depth of classification failure relative to a chosen invariant. A \emph{shadow map} records visible structure while suppressing finer information; lift packages recover this information in successive layers, and lift height measures the depth through which classification ambiguity persists. Canonical reduction removes redundant stages and yields an essential notion of lift height. For nilpotent groups, the lower central series provides a natural commutator lift tower, with lift height controlled by nilpotency class and decreasing under refinement of the shadow. The associated graded structure gives a Lie-theoretic interpretation of the successive commutator layers. The main examples show that classification depth is genuinely unbounded. Over any field of characteristic different from two, and for every positive integer, there exist nilpotent Lie algebras with the same fixed four-dimensional abelianisation whose commutator lift packages agree through the prescribed number of layers but differ at the next layer. Moreover, such separation can occur at arbitrarily large degree even when the complete underlying lower-central graded vector space is fixed. Thus neither a fixed shadow nor the dimensions, or even the underlying vector-space structure, of the lower-central graded object impose a uniform bound on the depth at which new commutator information may appear.
item.dc:creator: Joe Gildea

item.title: Division ring extensions and the realization of Coxeter diagrams $I_2(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $n\ge5$, we construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(n)$. Both of its diagonal division rings are two-generated over the field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$, where $\zeta$ is a primitive root of unity of order $n-2$. The construction is based on a chain of quantized Weyl relations and a shift automorphism. We give one-sided bases for the corresponding division ring extensions and compute the right dimension sequence of the bimodule. The resulting ring has exactly $n$ isomorphism classes of indecomposable finitely generated right modules.
item.dc:creator: A. I. Generalov, A. Tursunbaev

item.title: Becker's Conjecture on Compositions of Higher Degree Diagonal Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Becker's conjecture asserts that a rational composition of sums of $d$-th powers of size $[r,s,n]$, with $d>2$, requires $n \ge rs$. We show that this formulation fails over every characteristic-zero field in odd degree, and in every degree over a suitable finite extension of $\Q$. Over formally real fields in even degree, however, we prove that every polynomial composition satisfies $n\ge rs$.
item.dc:creator: Hua-Lin Huang, Yiming Liu, Huajun Lu, Yilun Tang

item.title: Nonassociative gradings on infinite-dimensional triangular algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study group gradings on triangular algebras relative to a well-ordered basis, with multiplication $x\circ_\lambda y=xy+\lambda yx$. For $\lambda\notin\{0,\pm1\}$, every grading on a finite-dimensional triangular algebra is isomorphic to an elementary grading. In infinite dimension, the same conclusion holds for the algebra of finite-range maps, for the finite-map algebra on a basis of order type $\omega$, and for closed gradings on the full triangular algebra. The infinite-dimensional results also hold for $\lambda=1$ in characteristic different from $2$. For intermediate algebras whose finite-range ideal is graded, we obtain an elementary description relative to a unitriangular basis. The proofs construct neutral associative idempotents with singleton diagonal supports. We also prove that the radical of the full triangular algebra is graded for every nonzero $\lambda$, and that gradings on the finite-range algebra and closed gradings on the full algebra have finite support under the classification hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Plamen Koshlukov, Waldeck Sch\"utzer, Felipe Yasumura

item.title: On semigroups of order-decreasing partial isometries: presentations and ranks of certain ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.12150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the monoid of all order-decreasing partial isometries on a chain with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{ODP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the submonoid of $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ consisting of all order-preserving partial isometries. In this paper, for each $1\leq r\leq n$, we determine minimal generating sets of the ideals $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$, thereby determining their ranks. Furthermore, we give presentations for the monoids $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$.
item.dc:creator: Gonca Ay\i k, Hayrullah Ay\i k, V\'itor H. Fernandes

item.title: A Note on Similarity Classes From Atomic Factorizations in Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.12297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an example of a non-Archimedean valued skew field k, with elements a and b of distinct absolute value such that there are no p, q $\in$ k[x] (x a central indeterminate) such that (x -b)(x -a) = pq, p similar to x -a, and q similar to x -b. The obstruction lies in the non-existence of a solution in k to Sylvester's equation at -tb = 1. We also disprove a 1963 result by Cohn (also reproduced in Cohn's 2006 monograph), by constructing a domain with similar elements a and b with a an atom and b not a product of atoms (resp., a product of two atoms, one of them central).
item.dc:creator: Friedrich Wehrung (LMNO,UNICAEN)

item.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.12469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Teheux

item.title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$. Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits hexagons. For the central simple examples in which all root spaces are non-zero, we determine which ones are Tits-hexagonalizable; in certain cases, this imposes an additional balancing condition on the idempotent.
item.dc:creator: Tom De Medts, Michiel Smet

item.title: On the structural aspects of Convex Subhyperlattices under different orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.10526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nayak et al. (2025) introduced the concept of convex subhyperlattices of a strong join hyperlattice $\mathfrak{L}$ and demonstrated that the collection of all convex subhyperlattices, $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$, together with empty set, forms a lattice. In particular, for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices, they obtained a unique representation of convex subhyperlattices in terms of hyperideals and hyperfilters. In the present work, we extend these studies by proving that $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L}) \cup \{\emptyset\}$, under set inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice. Moreover, we introduce two new orders on $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$ and examine their properties, including conditions for equivalence of these orders. In the class of $P$-hyperlattices, we characterize convex subhyperlattices in terms of initial and final segments, providing a structural insight into their formation. When convexity is extended to arbitrary join hyperlattices, many results known for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices fail to hold. To address these limitations of convexity in arbitrary hyperlattices, we introduce the notion of strongly convex sets, denoted $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$, which naturally generalizes the concept while preserving its fundamental properties and extends the applicability of results to a wider setting. We establish several results for $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$ that do not hold for $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$.
item.dc:creator: N Aishwarya Nayak, Bhargava K, Pallavi Panjarike, Kuncham Syam Prasad, Tapatee Sahoo, Harikrishnan Panackal

item.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Afifurrahman, Wildan Bagus Wicaksono

item.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yunmeng Wu, Milen Yakimov

item.title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.11900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko, Farukh Mashurov, Bauyrzhan Sartayev

item.title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.
item.dc:creator: Hongxing Chen

item.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.12495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries, Joris van der Hoeven

item.title: On $\mathrm{HH}^1$ of blocks of finite simple group algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a sporadic simple group, $k$ a field of positive characteristic and assume $B$ is a block of $kG$ with non-trivial defect. In this paper we prove the first Hochschild cohomology group $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is non-vanishing. Furthermore, we prove that for every wild block with abelian defect of a sporadic simple group, we have that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is a solvable Lie algebra of derived length two, with non-zero maximal toral rank.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Antrobus, Lleonard Rubio y Degrassi, Can Wen

item.title: Global structure behind pointwise equivalences of noncommutative polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2505.07469v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the interplay between local and global equivalences on noncommutative polynomials, the elements of the free algebra. When the latter are viewed as functions in several matrix variables, a local equivalence of noncommutative polynomials refers to their values sharing a common feature point-wise on matrix tuples of all dimensions, such as rank-equivalence (values have the same ranks), isospectrality (values have the same spectrum), and pointwise similarity (values are similar). On the other hand, a global equivalence refers to a ring-theoretic relation within the free algebra, such as stable association or (elementary) intertwinedness. This paper identifies the most ubiquitous pairs of local and global equivalences. Namely, rank-equivalence coincides with stable association, isospectrality coincides with both intertwinedness and transitive closure of elementary intertwinedness, and pointwise similarity coincides with equality. Using these characterizations, further results on spectral radii and norms of values of noncommutative polynomials are derived.
item.dc:creator: Eli Shamovich, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}

item.title: Cohomology and homotopy theory of Nijenhuis family algebras
item.description: arXiv:2508.17529v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nijenhuis family algebras generalize Nijenhuis associative algebras, the operator being replaced by a family of operators labelled by a semigroup $\Omega$. In this paper, we introduce Nijenhuis family bimodules and show that a Nijenhuis family algebra gives rise to an associative algebra on ${A\ot\bk\Omega}$. We realize Nijenhuis families and Nijenhuis family algebras as Maurer--Cartan elements of a graded Lie algebra and of an $L_\infty$-algebra. We define the cohomology of a Nijenhuis family algebra with coefficients in a bimodule via a mapping cone, obtain a long exact sequence, and show that infinitesimal deformations are classified by the second cohomology group. Finally, we show that strict homotopy Nijenhuis family algebras induce $A_\infty$-algebras on ${A\ot\bk\Omega}$.
item.dc:creator: Sami Benabdelhafidh

item.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
item.description: arXiv:2601.19698v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Marco Manetti, Gabriele Rossetti

item.title: $n$-Centers of Principal Subalgebras $\mathbb K Q_{\geq 1}$ of Path Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.23024v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero, we determine the $St_n$-elements and $n$-centers, defined by standard polynomials, of principal subalgebras of path algebras. Our description expresses each $n$-center as the direct sum of a path ideal and explicit subspaces associated with isolated circles. We prove that these $n$-centers are subalgebras and stabilize for $n\geq2|Q_0|$. We also obtain explicit descriptions of the center and the $3$-center, and determine the least degree of a standard polynomial identity in the acyclic case. Further applications concern algebras of block formal languages and rational Hilbert series of the $n$-centers.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: Local (Anti-)Superderivations on Finite-dimensional Nilpotent Lie Superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.00393v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study local superderivations and local anti-superderivations of finite-dimensional nilpotent Lie superalgebras over a field $\mathbb F$ with $\operatorname{char}\mathbb F\neq2$. First, we prove that every finite-dimensional two-step nilpotent Lie superalgebra admits pure local superderivations and pure local anti-superderivations (namely, local (anti-)superderivations that are not (anti-)superderivations). For nilpotent Lie superalgebras of nilpotency index greater than two, we establish sufficient conditions for the existence of pure local superderivations and pure local anti-superderivations. In particular, we prove that every three-step nilpotent Lie superalgebra admits a pure local superderivation.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohui Chi, Huiyi Zhang, Lingxin Meng, Liming Tang

item.title: Locally Closed Prime Ideals and Isotropy Induction in Kumjian--Pask Algebras over Commutative Rings
item.description: arXiv:2609.20230v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative unital ring and let $\Gamma$ be a row-finite, strongly aperiodic higher-rank graph with no sources and a nonempty finite vertex set. We determine the prime ideals that occur as annihilators of modules induced from simple isotropy modules. They are parametrised by maximal tails of $\Gamma$ and prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ for which the fraction field of $R/\mathfrak p$ is obtained by inverting a single element. Under the product description of the prime spectrum, these are precisely its locally closed points. The realisation argument uses a dense periodic orbit in every finite maximal-tail quotient. We also construct an explicit faithful simple module for the Leavitt algebra $L_R(1,2)$ whenever $R$ is a Goldman domain. Consequently, $L_{k[t]_{(t)}}(1,2)$ is primitive although its coefficient ring is not a field. In this example the zero ideal is locally closed but not completely irreducible. We obtain full prime-to-primitive coincidence for coefficient rings with finite spectrum and for semilocal rings of Krull dimension at most one, and transfer the results to split pullback Kumjian--Pask algebras. For pullbacks over an uncountable field, the full primitive spectrum is described without assuming algebraic closedness.
item.dc:creator: Bich Van Nguyen

item.title: When is the twist of a Leavitt path algebra again a Leavitt path algebra?
item.description: arXiv:2609.24836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study Zhang twist of Leavitt path algebra $L_K(E)$ using a graded automorphism $\sigma$ induced by a graph automorphism such that the twisted algebra is a Leavitt path algebra over another graph $E_{\sigma}$ which is a twisted graph obtained from the original graph $E$. We also show that the hypothesis that $\sigma$ be induced by a graph automorphism cannot be dropped as we construct a graded automorphism of the Leavitt path algebra of an infinite graph whose Zhang twist is not isomorphic to any Leavitt path algebra. We also define the notion of noncommutative projective scheme for $\mathbb Z$-graded algebras that coincides with the notion of noncommutative projective scheme for connected $\mathbb N$-graded algebras defined by Artin and Zhang and study it in the context of twists of Leavitt path algebras. We establish combinatorial connection between the graphs $E$ and $E_{\sigma}$ and as a consequence, we show that many ring-theoretic properties are invariant for Leavitt path algebras under the twist by $\sigma$. In particular, we show that the invariant basis number property is preserved under Zhang twists considered here for finite graphs, whereas the module type is not preserved.
item.dc:creator: Tran Giang Nam, Ashish K Srivastava

item.title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.08135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.
item.dc:creator: Jiamei Li, Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng

item.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Karan Choudhary, Sunil Kumar Prajapati

item.title: Almost Symmetric Linear Arc Monadic Datalog and Transitive Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2606.24711v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce $n$-almost symmetric Datalog and study $n$-almost symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog. We characterize the finite relational structures whose constraint satisfaction problem is solved by this Datalog fragment as those that can be primitive positively constructed from the transitive tournament on $n+2$ vertices. We also give characterizations in terms of a certain homomorphism duality (which we call $n$-fixed unfolded caterpillar duality) and in universal-algebraic terms (the existence of $k$-absorptive operations and of operations forming an elevator chain of length $n+1$). This article generalizes the results from Bodirsky and Starke about symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Meyer, Florian Starke

item.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and their related binary LCD codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ which attains the asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov bound, i.e., whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/2)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with previously unknown parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$ and nine binary LCD codes with the best known parameters.
item.dc:creator: Xingxing Xu, Bo Wu, Jon-Lark Kim

item.title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
item.description: arXiv:2610.34119v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $\Omega(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense. We also identify a gap in an earlier proof of its nonstandardness and give an independent proof by determining all connected Galois covering sources of $\Omega(1)$. Together, these results disprove the implication from Euclidean type to standardness in the equivalence explicitly stated by Bocian--Holm--Skowro\'nski (2004) and Bocian--Skowro\'nski (2005). They also contradict the standardness conclusion of the Proposition in \S2.1 of Skowro\'nski (1989); its main theorem in \S1.5 assumes standardness and is not contradicted by this example.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba
